source_refs.note: Fluoroquinolones (printed '23.2.3.'; PDF 211). The book credits Lesher (1962) with discovering fluoroquinolones; a note explains that he found the first quinolone, from which fluoroquinolones were later made.

blocks.text: Fluoroquinolones are synthetic antibacterial agents, bactericidal antibiotics that treat infections by inhibiting bacterial DNA replication. They are derived as a by-product of the synthesis of chloroquine, itself a synthetic modification of quinine, an alkaloid from the bark of the South American Cinchona tree, and were discovered by George Lesher in 1962. They are linked with significant though rare side effects, including tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy and heart problems, and with drug resistance.

items: Bactericidal: they trap the enzymes of DNA replication in a complex that causes double-strand DNA breaks, so the bacteria cannot multiply and die.
They enter bacterial cells and inhibit type II topoisomerases.
In Gram-positive bacteria they mainly target topoisomerase IV, stopping the separation of replicated DNA.
In Gram-negative bacteria they mainly target DNA gyrase, stopping the uncoiling of DNA during replication.
